leads.name: Tomnahurich Cemetery yews
leads.reason: Gaelic name 'hill of the yews'; Ancient Yew Group Highland survey (Andy Moffat PDF) lists yews but names no individual ancient tree or girth; no pin, no measurement. Cemetery is open. No photo or exact pin in reach.

leads.name: Yews on and around Ness Islands
leads.reason: Same Ancient Yew Group PDF lists several yews, no ages, none marked ancient; Victorian pleasure ground (bridges 1828). No individual tree identified.

leads.name: Cawdor Castle old yew
leads.reason: ancient-yew.org record 5276: 1834 guide describes an ancient yew in the castle garden, site says it is not known whether it survives; castle gardens are paid entry; no girth. Alive not shown.

leads.name: Reelig Glen other giant Douglas firs
leads.reason: Folded into rlg_001; Wikipedia says several trees in the glen exceed 55 m, a few exceed 60 m, no individual named.

leads.name: Culloden House old trunk
leads.reason: OS name book (1876-78, Highland HER MHG2951 'Brangas Tree') records a withered ivy-covered trunk on the lawn of Culloden House; the house is a hotel, grounds not confirmed open, and it was not read. Possibly long gone.

leads.name: Dornoch yews
leads.reason: Ancient Yew Group PDF: a number of small to medium sized yews in Dornoch; nothing remarkable named.

blocked.name: Beauly Priory wych elm
blocked.reason: Dead: the 800-year-old wych elm fell on 5 January 2023 after Dutch elm disease (Inverness Courier, Press and Journal reports in search results); two young elms planted 29 April 2024, one on the spot. Coordinate near 57.4806,-4.4720 not fetched.
